messages:
ella_sales: Hey team — POC with AcmeCorp hitting weird structured-output failures in JSON mode. Customer says the function call payload is getting truncated and then parsing fails on their side. Can we swarm? :eyes:

sam_se: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the exact model request + headers and the error they see? Also which model/config (quant, max_tokens, json_mode) are you using?

customer_jr: Posting example we got from our backend. They say first ~512 tokens look fine then we get:
```
Error: invalid JSON: unexpected end of input at char 1023
raw snippet: "{\"items\": [{\"id\": \"123\", \"desc\": \"Line one\\nLine two\"}, {\"id\": \"124\", \"desc\": \"Some text with escape \\\" sequences..."
```
We tried increasing max_tokens but still cuts mid-string.

sam_se: Thanks. Two quick checks: are you using `json_mode: true` (the endpoint-level structured output) or are you doing `function_call`? They behave differently w.r.t. truncation and stop sequences. Also share the request_id from headers if available.

ella_sales: It's `json_mode: true` with a schema. Model: `open-instruct-XXL` pinned, quant config `int8`, max_tokens 2048, but most calls hit ~1100 tokens then break. request_id from response: `r-0a9c3f2d`.

arjun_eng: Jumping in from runtime — that request_id maps to a server-side 413-like advisory: we saw client-side truncation triggered by the per-connection chunk limit on the load balancer. Running logs show the stream closed with `EPIPE` after 1.1k tokens. Looks like the streaming buffer and our JSON chunker didn't flush the final `]}` in time.

sam_se: Can you paste the minimal logs? Also, are you using automatic prefix KV caching or custom prompts with a lot of escape sequences (`\\n`, `\\"`)? Those increase token estimates.

arjun_eng: Logs for r-0a9c3f2d:
```
[2026-02-15T17:12:03Z] conn 1987: stream write 1120/1120 -> closed (EPIPE)
[2026-02-15T17:12:03Z] model open-instruct-XXL: tokenized_len=1132, max_allowed=2048, batch_flush=1024
[2026-02-15T17:12:03Z] json-mode: buffered_bytes=10176, flush_deadline_missed=true
```
Looks like our batch flush threshold (1024) + socket chunking caused premature close. We need to bump continuous-batch flush to avoid mid-JSON truncation.

customer_jr: Is that something we can toggle on our side? We don't control your runtime. Customer is sensitive to changing model/quant.

marta_security: Also flagging security side: are any of the truncated fragments leaking sensitive tokens or PII in logs? We should rotate any keys if logs contained tokens.

ella_sales: Good catch — customer used UIDs but no secrets in payload. They asked about retry semantics: if we retry at our side will they see duplicate events? They currently parse once and store.

arjun_eng: Two recommended short-term actions: 1) enable `streaming: false` for JSON mode calls (server will synthesize full JSON then return) — avoids chunking issues at cost of latency; 2) increase runtime `batch_flush` threshold for this customer's dedicated pool to 4096 bytes (we can do this from Dedicated config).

sam_se: For the customer-facing guidance: tell them to set `max_wait_for_stream_end_ms: 10000` in their HTTP client and to validate JSON strictly before persistence. We'll coordinate with infra to change flush for the POC.

customer_jr: Ok we can set client timeout and add strict JSON check on our end. Can you do the flush change and let us know ETA?

arjun_eng: I'll open an infra change and tag it to this thread. ETA ~ 2 hours to apply to their dedicated pool and run smoke tests. Will post logs after patch.

deploy-bot: infra-change rfc#4527 applied to pool `acme-poc` — config update queued. CI smoke run starting. :rocket:

sam_se: One more: I saw `invalid escape sequence` in the customer's snippet — encourage them to run `jsonlint` on the generated string before sending to their parser. The root cause is almost always truncation + embedded `\\n`/`\\"` sequences.

marta_security: After patch, we'll scrub logs and confirm no PII persisted. If any sensitive fragments were stored by the customer, they should rotate.

ella_sales: Great — please @arjun_eng and @sam_se tag me once done. I'll tell the customer we're on it and they should add the timeout + jsonlint as a stopgap. :thumbsup:
